clue.text: Car firm and corporation from the East …

parts.note: firm means hard, as in solid

indicators.note: in an across clue, coming from the east means read right to left, so the word is turned round

parts.note: corporation is slang for a pot belly, a pot

explanation.surface: A clue about a car company and a corporation from the Orient, trailing off into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis joins this clue to the next only for the surface. 'Corporation' is the old joke for a big belly.
explanation.definitionFit: A car with a rigid roof is a type of motor vehicle, the opposite of a convertible.

clue.text: Horse that's longed to get married

parts.note: H is slang for heroin, horse
to itch for something is to long for it

explanation.surface: A horse that has longed to tie the knot.
explanation.walkthrough: H for horse comes via heroin: both are slang names for the drug.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting hitched is an informal idiom for getting wed.

clue.text: Swimmer making agent lose head

indicators.note: lose head means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: a broker is an agent who buys and sells for others

explanation.surface: A swimmer whose agent is about to be beheaded.
explanation.definitionFit: The roker is a ray, a flat fish, and fish are swimmers in crossword terms.

clue.text: Did this in empty tube after shot and wine?

indicators.note: after puts the emptied tube following the shot

parts.note: a shot of spirits is a tot

indicators.note: empty removes the inner letters, keeping just the outside pair

parts.note: red is a colour of wine

explanation.surface: Someone on the underground, the Tube, after a spirit and wine, staggering along.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue also reads as a whole: after a shot and some wine, this is what you did on the empty Tube.
explanation.definitionFit: The definition is the drunken action described, walking unsteadily.

clue.text: Green space vessel with bit of pink on top

indicators.note: in a down answer, on top means placed above the vessel word
bit of picks just the opening letter of the colour

parts.note: Noah's ark was a vessel

explanation.surface: A space-age green vessel with pink trimming on top.
explanation.definitionFit: A public garden or grassy area in a town is a green open area.

clue.text: … studied safe reversing in training day

indicators.note: in tells us the turned word sits inside the other letters

parts.note: PE, physical education, is training of the body

indicators.note: reversing tells us the word for safe runs backwards here

parts.note: safe means sure, as in a safe bet

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: something studied the safe being backed up on a training day.
explanation.walkthrough: SURE turned by 'reversing' gives ERUS, which goes 'in' PE and D.
explanation.definitionFit: To peruse is to read or examine carefully, a synonym of having studied.

clue.text: Broadcast loop with static coming after it?

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered about, so the letters are spread into a new order

explanation.surface: A radio loop of static that follows a broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' is the old euphemism for sex, so coming after it means after intercourse.
explanation.definitionFit: The word describes the time after sex, which the clue coyly calls 'it'.

clue.text: Royal and bishop engulfed by a little gas

indicators.note: engulfed by means surrounded, so the bishop letter goes inside

parts.note: a little is a bit
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A royal and a bishop overcome by a small amount of gas.
explanation.walkthrough: To rabbit is British slang for chatting on endlessly, as is gas.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are informal verbs meaning to chatter idly.

clue.text: Arts paper blasted "mechanical understudy"

indicators.note: blasted means blown apart, so the letters are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: A newspaper arts section slating a machine-like stand-in actor.
explanation.definitionFit: A replacement component kept ready for a machine is like an understudy waiting to step in.

clue.text: Met to green-light advert about old planes

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the whole string reads backwards

parts.note: met, as a committee meets, means sat
to green-light is to approve, to OK
an ad is an advert

explanation.surface: A meeting called to approve an advertising campaign.
explanation.walkthrough: SATOKAD read back by 'about' gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Douglas DC-3 transport aircraft of the 1940s was known by this name in RAF service.

clue.text: Follow one another around in Turkestan

indicators.note: around suggests the letters of the place name are moved about into a new order

explanation.surface: Travellers following each other on a tour of Turkestan, a region of Central Asia.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing things in alternation means each person follows the other, an idiomatic sense.

clue.text: Line adopted by champion chess player

indicators.note: adopted by means taken in by the other word, so one sits inside

parts.note: to champion a cause is to back it

explanation.surface: A particular line of play taken up by a chess champion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Champion' looks like a noun beside 'chess player' but is the verb, to support.
explanation.definitionFit: In chess one side plays the dark pieces, so the player of those pieces is named by their colour.

clue.text: Game Chuck Yeager's first to neck drug

indicators.note: to neck is to swallow, so the drug goes inside the other letters

parts.note: to chuck is to throw, to hurl

indicators.note: first picks just the opening letter of the pilot's surname

parts.note: E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Chuck Yeager, the American test pilot, knocking back drugs: a scandal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chuck' looks like Yeager's first name, but it is the verb to throw.
explanation.definitionFit: Hurley is a name for the Irish stick-and-ball sport hurling, as well as the stick itself.

clue.text: Stress over independent daughter's mishap

indicators.note: over means the stress word covers the other letters, which sit inside it

parts.note: stress on a syllable is its accent
D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A stressful worry about a daughter's independence after some misfortune.
explanation.definitionFit: An accident is an unlucky event, a synonym of mishap.

clue.text: City star embarrassed travelling up to Settle

parts.note: the sun is a star

indicators.note: in a down answer, travelling up means the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: an embarrassed face goes red
to settle, as a bird does, is to land

explanation.surface: A city star blushing as he heads up to the town of Settle in Yorkshire.
explanation.walkthrough: Settle is a small town in North Yorkshire, but here it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A city in north-east England, on the River Wear.

clue.text: Is Camden University happy about disco?

indicators.note: happy suggests the letters are in a lively, loosened state and so rearranged

parts.note: C, for circa, is the abbreviation for about

explanation.surface: Asking whether the university in Camden, north London, is pleased with its disco.
explanation.walkthrough: Camden is a district of north London.
explanation.definitionFit: Disco is a genre of dance-floor pop, an example of the wider category of club music.

clue.text: Trouble due at sea after head of navy revolted

indicators.note: after puts the jumbled letters behind the navy letter
head of picks the opening letter of the word
trouble means disturb, so the letters are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: Trouble at sea expected after a naval chief mutinied.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolted' suggests a mutiny but means disgusted.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling sick with disgust is to be revolted, a synonym.

clue.text: Caught when stashing last of eight ounces?

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: stashing means hiding something away inside

parts.note: as means when, as in 'as I arrived'

indicators.note: last of picks the final letter of the number word

explanation.surface: A smuggler caught with eight ounces of something hidden on them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ounces' looks like a weight; an ounce is also the snow leopard, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: The snow leopard is also called the ounce, so ounces are big felines.

clue.text: Evil woman of the cloth ringing home

indicators.note: ringing means encircling, so the nun word goes round the home word

parts.note: a sister is a nun, a woman in holy orders
in means at home

explanation.surface: A wicked nun telephoning home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ringing' suggests a phone call, but means surrounding.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinister means threatening harm, a synonym of evil.

clue.text: Union card

definitions.meaning: an association of members joined together, a society
a playing card of the suit marked with a black trefoil

explanation.definitionFit: Both a society of members and one of the four suits of playing cards share this word.

clue.text: Drug story sat on by daily

indicators.note: in a down answer, sat on by puts the cleaner word above the story word

parts.note: a daily, or char, is a British cleaner who comes in every day
a story is a lie, a fib

explanation.surface: A newspaper drug story suppressed by a daily paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Daily' looks like a newspaper; a daily is an old British name for a domestic cleaner.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for cocaine, a well-known drug.

clue.text: Romantic aid elicits barking

indicators.note: barking is British slang for mad, so the letters go wild into a new order

explanation.surface: Help that draws out a dog's bark, read as a romantic gesture.
explanation.definitionFit: A romantic is one who holds lofty, unrealistic ideals, so the two adjectives are synonyms.

clue.text: Covers accountant delivers in a melodic way?

parts.note: CA, chartered accountant
to deliver words melodically is to sing them

explanation.surface: An accountant delivering a report with a tune in his voice.
explanation.definitionFit: Casings are outer shells, which cover what lies within.

clue.text: Revolutionary lets out inspiring old druggie

indicators.note: inspiring means breathing in, so the old letter is taken inside
revolutionary means turning round, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: a landlord who lets out rooms rents them

explanation.surface: A revolutionary freeing an inspirational old drug user.
explanation.definitionFit: A stoner is slang for one who habitually smokes cannabis, a druggie.

clue.text: Opening time in a country bar came at last

indicators.note: in places the time letter inside the country name

parts.note: Peru is a country in South America

indicators.note: at last picks the final letter of each of the two words before it

explanation.surface: Opening time in a bar abroad, when the drinker finally arrived.
explanation.definitionFit: An aperture is a hole or gap, a synonym of opening as a noun.

clue.text: Those digging The Young Ones on radio?

indicators.note: on radio means as heard spoken, so a word with the same sound

parts.note: young ones under legal age are minors

explanation.surface: Fans of the cult comedy The Young Ones hearing it broadcast on radio.
explanation.walkthrough: The Young Ones was a 1980s British TV sitcom; here it just means youngsters.
explanation.definitionFit: People who work underground extracting coal are, literally, those who dig.

clue.text: Supply joke from the internet?

parts.note: E, as in e-mail, means electronic or online
a quip is a witty joke

explanation.surface: Providing a joke taken from the web.
explanation.definitionFit: To equip is to furnish with what is needed, a synonym of supply.

clue.text: What Big Sam is to those under him? A stud

definitions.text: What Big Sam is to those under him?
definitions.meaning: Big Sam is Sam Allardyce, a football manager, the gaffer to his players
a raised knob or stud, as on a shield

explanation.walkthrough: Big Sam is the nickname of Sam Allardyce, an English football manager.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a manager over employees and a raised ornamental knob.

clue.text: Can following learner lead to awful language?

indicators.note: following puts the container word after the others

parts.note: L is the learner driver's plate

indicators.note: lead to picks the leading letter of the next word

parts.note: a can is a tin

explanation.surface: Asking whether a learner's foul language follows from a can of drink.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient tongue of Rome, one of the classical languages.

clue.text: A fit type performing brief role reversal

parts.note: a fit of illness is a bout
a turn is a performer doing a short act on a variety bill

explanation.surface: A fit actor playing a short part that is a role reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: A complete change of direction or policy, a military-drill idiom for a reversal.

clue.text: Before onset of unconsciousness, butt ruddy bore

indicators.note: before places the butt word ahead of the following letter

parts.note: the butt is the end of something, as of a cigarette

indicators.note: onset of picks the opening letter of the word

parts.note: ruddy means red in colour

explanation.surface: A boxer's blow knocking out a dull ruddy-faced bore before he passes out.
explanation.definitionFit: Bore is the past tense of bear, to tolerate, a synonym of the answer.

clue.text: Some kits will carry these at the side

definitions.text: Some kits will carry these at the side

parts.words: Some kits will carry these at the side
parts.note: football kits often have long coloured lines down the sides; kits are also kittens, and tabby kittens have markings

explanation.definitionFit: Sports kits and tabby kittens alike bear long bands of colour along their flanks.
